name: Grunge. Supplemental design reference from the Graphic Design and Design Movements category. The source does not list it as a directly named style in its collection.
visualIdentity: Worn surfaces with distressed ink, scratches, stains, incomplete lettering, and rough substrates. Texture density and scale stay controlled so the message remains clear. Local erasures and surface reveals replace whole-frame darkening or persistent noise over the subject.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to texture-led title sequences and mood pieces used alone. The source suggests music promos, documentary chapter titles, gritty brand statements, atmospheric intros, and album visualizers. Glitch-cut transitions list Grunge as a good fit.
limitations: The worn surface must stay primary, and supporting styles are added only for paced typography or spatial depth. Avoid full-frame persistent noise over text, whole-frame darkening, bouncy text easing, and exposed texture edges. Rough.js hachure does not create authentic pencil, print, or ink-wash media. Duration, resolution, and aspect ratio are unspecified; the source offers them only as optional examples.
palette: Status is a style-compatible suggestion, applying only to new artwork when no approved palette is supplied. Roles are background #E4DCCD (worn paper), foreground #302E29 (charcoal), and accent_1 #8C5140 (oxidized red). Gradients are disabled. Task or brand colors override these, and assets must not be recolored or given added hues.
motionAndInteraction: Motion should reveal textures locally and stay coherent with a single timeline owner. Smooth easing is used where it helps, while sharp cuts, impacts, and reading holds are preserved. Suggested patterns include chaptered transitions, scroll-driven storytelling, and glitch cuts, each optional and chosen only when the scene supports it. Video uses seekable composition time, while live scroll or pointer input belongs only to interactive delivery.
audio: The source gives no Grunge-specific audio direction. Music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence should be chosen from the brief, and explicit user audio requirements take priority. Speech must stay intelligible without competing vocals or clipping. Any sound accent should align with phrase breaks or key transitions.
assetRequirements: Precompute distressed masks, ink textures, and paper grain, then reuse the same textures identically on every render. Load local fonts and assets before rendering, and seed any randomness. Supplied source artwork, exact colors, and approved assets must remain intact. No specific asset list is provided, so missing assets are unspecified and must be stated.
combinations: Grunge works alone for texture-led title sequences and mood pieces. Typography sequencing with style-093 reveals distressed headline words one at a time, with only the active word distressed. Background depth with style-101 uses three texture planes in slow parallax, keeping foreground motion within about twice background speed and overscanning all artwork.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default composition and export pipeline, and Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation applies, with the reason recorded. Canvas 2D handles visual construction, Rough.js is optional for sketch marks, and GSAP owns motion on a paused timeline. Pillow and Python preprocess textures. Validation covers key frames, the full watched video, dimensions, and audio sync before delivery.
